title: The North Face Dome 8 review: the hub-pole storm dome before the 2-Meter Dome
dek: An eight-person, four-season dome with a ring-shaped aluminum hub, three double doors and an 83-inch peak. It's slow to pitch and very hard to hurt.
subject: The North Face Dome 8
verdict: The Dome 8 is an overbuilt, stand-up basecamp dome that owners trust in severe storms. Its hub-and-pole frame and many inner-tent connectors make setup slow, and it was replaced by the 2-Meter Dome. A used one in good shape is still a serious group shelter.
bestFor: Group basecamps, long stays in severe weather, campers who want full standing room.
notFor: Beginners, solo setup, or ordinary campground trips where a lighter tent would do.
pros: Owner reports it stayed dry and intact in 80+ mph winds and hail
83 in peak and about 128 sq ft of floor
Three double doors and a 34 sq ft vestibule
Ring-shaped aluminum hub simplifies the frame
cons: Owner reports about 1.5 hours to pitch the first time
Many small inner-tent connectors and a confusing manual
Heavy, with a 35 lb packed weight
Discontinued, so parts come from surplus stock
body:
## The short version

The Dome 8 was The North Face's eight-person, four-season basecamp dome before the 2-Meter Dome replaced it. It stands 83 inches at the peak, covers about 128 square feet, and has three double doors plus a 34-square-foot vestibule. The frame uses DAC poles joined by a ring-shaped aluminum hub.

## Weather

The owner review on Trailspace is the kind you want for a storm tent. During an Oklahoma thunderstorm with winds over 80 mph, dime-sized hail and nearly four inches of rain in an hour, the owner stayed dry and the tent came through without damage. Their description: bulletproof, and overbuilt for typical U.S. camping.

## Setup

The same owner is just as clear about setup: about an hour and a half the first time, with two people. The inner tent hangs from many small connectors, some poles had to be redone despite the color coding, and they found the manual poor. Once you've learned it, it goes faster, but this isn't a tent for beginners or for pitching alone.

## Who it suits now

With full standing height and three doors, the Dome 8 is comfortable for older campers and big groups who want room to move. It shines on long basecamp stays and in places where storms are a real threat.

## Poles and parts

The Dome 8 uses **a hubbed pole set** (several legs joined at an aluminum hub), **DAC**.

The hub is the heart of the frame. If you're buying a used Dome 8, check that the hub isn't cracked and that every pole leg seats fully into it.

The North Face doesn't publish pole lengths. To match a replacement, lay your pole out straight, measure tip to tip, count the sections, and read the diameter printed near a joint (or use calipers). Then search the Dome 8 in our [pole and parts finder](/poles?model=Dome%208), compare against measured stock in the [pole size chart](/poles/sizes), or search by measurement in [find a pole by size](/poles/size).

## Bottom line

A used Dome 8 is a lot of storm tent for the money. Budget time to learn the pitch, and check the hub, pole ends and inner-tent connectors before you buy.
